Method of Attack: Injected malicious code that tampers with package.json, injects local scripts, republishes altered tarballs to trojanize downstream projects
Malicious bundle.js downloads TruffleHog secret scanner, profiles host, scans files and repos for tokens and cloud credentials
Validates and reuses developer/cloud credentials, drops GitHub Actions workflow using any available PAT, exfiltrates secrets to hardcoded webhook
Fetches platform-specific TruffleHog binaries, executes locally to automate secret theft and repository compromise
Scans hosts and repos for environment secrets (GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, AWS keys), probes cloud metadata endpoints (AWS/GCP) to harvest short-lived credentials
Plants persistent GitHub Actions workflow in repositories to exfiltrate secrets and artifacts on future CI runs
Attack Vector: Malicious package update published to npm registry
Supply chain attack via compromised npm packages
Exploitation of developer tokens and cloud credentials
Injection of malicious GitHub Actions workflows
Indicators of Compromise: Exfiltration of base64 encoded secrets to hardcoded webhook
Presence of GitHub Actions workflows planted by malware
Use of environment variables like GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, AWS keys
Verification of npm tokens via whoami endpoint
